limits: Online docs were read as requirements/reference material. They are not evidence of actual lifecycle state during the original run. No source implementation was obtained from competitors or imported from documentation.

references.supports: Window key status can be observed through public become/resign-key notifications; makeKeyAndVisible establishes key visibility at the call.
Key-window status is scoped to the scene on current iOS; the key window is the destination for keyboard and other non-touch events.
windowScene names the associated scene; a nil assignment removes that association. Selected runtime samples already show a scene.
The ordered list supplies the search for the default focused item; it does not define a Tab successor.
Heading none conveys no movement heading; it does not identify the cause of an update.
The nullable property can be unavailable when the scene does not support focus.
Scene lifecycle has public connect/disconnect, foreground/background and activate/deactivate notifications.
An onscreen foreground scene may be inactive and not receiving user events.
The public API types one physical-key representation with specified modifiers; return alone does not promise focus traversal.
Programmatic scene lifecycle setup creates a UIWindow associated with a UIWindowScene. This general direction does not prove the cause of the selected iOS26.5 failure.

scope: Primary Apple documentation read through web tool; summaries below are authored notes, not downloaded SDK content. Pinned local headers are bound separately.
